analysis.title: Equities Monthly, November 2026: AI wobble about deployment, not demand
key_insights: October marked a broadening in market leadership as crowded AI and mega-cap positions corrected, while defensive, value and previously lagging areas gained ground.
Fidelity expects the next phase to reward companies with resilient earnings, disciplined capital allocation and clear returns on investment, rather than exposure to structural growth themes alone.
AI demand persists, but physical bottlenecks could stretch the investment cycle. The October wobble is framed as about deployment, not demand.

US equities declined in October as investors rotated out of AI-linked growth stocks into value and defensive sectors. The S&P 500 fell while the Russell 1000 Value Index advanced, as a broad technology sell-off weighed on sentiment.
European equities advanced in October, outperforming US and global markets on positive earnings and strength in energy and defensive sectors, which offset late-month volatility.

Japanese equities weakened in October as concerns over the sustainability and financing of AI investment triggered profit-taking in crowded technology stocks. Higher global bond yields and renewed inflation concerns added to risk aversion.
UK equities rose in October, with the FTSE All Share gaining 1.1% on resilient activity and corporate earnings. Large-caps regained the lead over FTSE 250 and small caps.

Fidelity argues the UK discount is hard to ignore: valuations are attractive, sentiment is improving, shareholder returns are strong, and the market has more exposure to asset-backed businesses. It supports revisiting underweight UK allocations.
EM equities fell sharply in October and underperformed developed markets. Middle East tensions added to inflation and policy concerns. Brazil erased earlier gains after the election.

Asia-Pacific ex-Japan equities fell 6.9% in October on concerns over the sustainability and returns of AI investment, which triggered a broad technology sell-off and an unwind of crowded trades in Korea and Taiwan.

Fidelity's bottom-up FY26 earnings forecasts are most bullish versus consensus in Europe and most bearish in EM ex-Asia. IT and energy are the top sectors for earnings growth, healthcare and real estate the bottom.
The quantitative equities signal is Risk ON. The US S&P 500 drops to strong underweight on flows and technical signals, and Australia also drops to strong underweight.

Quant regional moves: Germany slips to neutral, Netherlands upgrades for a second month, Sweden downgrades again on weak momentum, Italy rises two spots to overweight, and Japan declines to neutral on short-term momentum and flow headwinds.

Quant US sector moves: staples upgrade to overweight on adjusted flows and equity borrowing, energy reverses last month's upgrade on weaker flows, materials climb to overweight, and real estate falls to strong underweight.

Quant Europe sector moves: communication services drop on deteriorating asset quality, discretionary moves to neutral, energy moves to overweight, industrials jump two spots to strong overweight, IT is neutral as net income growth softens, and real estate drops to strong underweight.

earnings_insights: Fidelity FY26 bottom-up earnings forecasts (Fidelity estimates, not reported results): most bullish versus consensus in Europe, most bearish in EM ex-Asia.

Fidelity FY26 sector earnings growth forecasts: IT 95%, energy 45%, materials 43%, communication services 35%, discretionary 22%, utilities 19%, industrials 14%, financials 12%, staples 8%, real estate 3%, healthcare 1%. These are Fidelity estimates.

Fidelity FY28 earnings growth estimates versus IBES consensus (Fidelity estimate): Global IT +6.9%, communication services +7.0%, industrials +3.5%, materials -11.0%, energy -5.2%. By region: US +3.0%, Europe -0.1%, APxJ +3.9%, Japan -1.6%, EMEA/LATAM -7.2%, China +0.3%, Global +2.1%.
risk_factors: Physical bottlenecks could stretch the AI investment cycle.
Concerns over the sustainability and financing of AI investment triggered the October technology sell-off, notably in Japan and Asia-Pacific ex-Japan.
Higher global bond yields and renewed inflation concerns added to risk aversion.
Middle East tensions add to inflation and policy concerns for EM.
vol_and_positioning: Crowded AI and mega-cap technology positions corrected in October, with leadership broadening toward value, defensive and previously lagging areas.
Crowded technology trades unwound across Asia, with Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, KOSPI and the Taiwan TAIEX among the decliners.
The quantitative equities signal is Risk ON, a 1-3 month view.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions added to inflation and policy concerns for EM equities in October.
Brazil equities erased earlier gains after the election.
